note: The syllabus for practice mode. Picked up front so the set has coverage rather than forty variations on map. Every string under `verified` is an observation from this engine (2.12.2-20260715) via scripts/practice/verify-traps*.mjs — not recollection. `trap` is the reason the unit is worth a question at all.

units.title: Pick fields out and build a new object
units.teaches: Selectors and object construction — the 80% of real DataWeave.
units.trap: A key that isn't there is `null`, not an error, so a typo ships silently.
verified: key order is preserved as written: { z: 1, a: 2, m: 3 } stays z,a,m

units.title: Transform every element of an array
units.teaches: `map`, the lambda form and the `$`/`$$` shorthand.
units.trap: `$$` is the index in `map` but the KEY in `mapObject` — same symbol, different thing.

units.title: Keep only the rows that qualify
units.teaches: `filter` and the difference between empty and absent.
units.trap: Every array function returns null for a null input instead of failing, so a wrong selector produces an empty-looking result rather than a stack trace.

units.title: Supply a fallback for a missing field
units.teaches: `default` and what actually counts as missing.
units.trap: `default` only fires on null. An empty string and `false` are values, and both pass straight through.

units.title: Clean up and recombine text
units.teaches: The string functions that appear in nearly every mapping.
units.trap: `splitBy` takes a String or a Regex and the two behave differently on a separator with regex meaning, such as `.` or `|`.

units.title: Money that adds up
units.teaches: Arithmetic and formatting a number for output.
units.trap: `/` is never integer division — `7 / 2` is `3.5`, and formatting it with `#` does not round it either.

units.title: First, last and the middle bit
units.teaches: Indexing and range selectors on arrays and strings.
units.trap: A negative index counts from the end rather than erroring, and an index past the end is null — so `[1,2,3][-1]` is 3 and `[1,2,3][9]` is null.

units.title: Join two lists, drop an entry
units.teaches: `++` and `--` across arrays, objects and strings.
units.trap: `++` will not mix kinds: appending a bare value to an array is a COMPILE error, not a silent push.

units.title: Bucket records by a field
units.teaches: `groupBy` and the shape it hands back.
units.trap: `groupBy` returns an OBJECT, not an array, and the grouping value is coerced to a String key — group by a number and your keys are "1" and "0".

units.title: Fold a list into one value
units.teaches: `reduce`, its argument order and the seed.
units.trap: With no seed, reducing an empty array gives null — so a total that is usually a number is occasionally null, and it only shows up on the day a filter matches nothing.

units.title: Turn an object into rows
units.teaches: Iterating an object rather than an array.
units.trap: `pluck` produces an array and `mapObject` produces an object; both hand you `(value, key, index)` — value FIRST, which is the opposite of how the pair reads out loud.

units.title: Two fields with the same name
units.teaches: That a DataWeave object is an ordered list of pairs, not a map.
units.trap: Duplicate keys are LEGAL and survive to the output — `{a:1} ++ {a:2}` keeps both — so a collision produces JSON that every downstream parser reads differently instead of failing here.
verified: payload mapObject { kind: $ } over two keys -> { 'kind': 1, 'kind': 2 }

units.title: Dedupe and sort a feed
units.teaches: `distinctBy`, `orderBy` and how to sort descending.
units.trap: There is no `orderBy desc` — you reverse with `[-1 to 0]`. And ordering a column with mixed types throws rather than sorting loosely.
verified: [3,'1',2] orderBy $ -> InvalidComparisonException: Types String and Number can not be compared

units.title: Collapse a list of lists
units.teaches: Flattening, and when `flatMap` says it better.
units.trap: `flatten` goes exactly one level deep — a doubly-nested array comes back still nested.

units.title: Include a field only when it applies
units.teaches: `(key: value) if (condition)` — omitting a key rather than emitting a null.
units.trap: The parentheses are part of the syntax; without them the `if` reads as part of the value and you get a null key instead of no key.

units.title: Change one field, keep the rest
units.teaches: `update ... with` / `update { case ... }` instead of rebuilding the whole object.
units.trap: Updating a key that does not exist is a silent no-op — it does not add it.

units.title: Strings that have to become numbers
units.teaches: `as Number`, `as Boolean`, and guarding a coercion.
units.trap: A blank string is not zero and 'yes' is not true — both throw at runtime, on the one record in ten thousand that has them.

units.title: A CSV in, a JSON out
units.teaches: Reader/writer properties: header, separator, quoting.
units.trap: Every value parsed from CSV is a String, including the ones that look like numbers, so arithmetic on them fails until you coerce.
verified: typeOf of a numeric-looking CSV column -> 'String'

units.title: Read a repeated XML element
units.teaches: `.`, `.*` and `@` on XML.
units.trap: `.` on a repeated element silently gives you only the FIRST one. `.*` gives all of them. A feed that usually has one child makes this bug invisible in testing.

units.title: Format a date the way the partner wants it
units.teaches: Format patterns for dates and times.
units.trap: The pattern letters are case-sensitive and three of them lie: `DD` is day-of-YEAR, `mm` is minutes, and `YYYY` is the ISO week-year — which disagrees with the calendar year at the end of December.

units.title: How long between these two timestamps?
units.teaches: Periods, `|P1D|` literals and pulling a number out of a duration.
units.trap: Subtracting two dates gives a Period, not a Number — and adding a month to the 31st clamps to the end of the shorter month rather than overflowing.

units.title: Branch on the shape of the data
units.teaches: `match` with `case x is Type`, guards, and `else`.
units.trap: Cases are tried in order and the first match wins, so a broad `is Number` above a specific guard makes the guard dead code.
verified: 5 match { case n is Number -> 'num' case a if (a > 0) -> 'pos' else -> 'other' } -> 'num'
list-destructuring patterns DO NOT PARSE: `case [h] ->` and `case [h, t...] ->` both give CompilationException: Invalid input "match { case [h,", expected Function Call
what works: `case x is Type`, `case x if (...)`, `case null`, `else`

units.title: Name an intermediate result
units.teaches: `do { var ... --- ... }` for a local binding inside an expression.
units.trap: A `var` at the header is computed once for the whole script; one inside a `do` inside a `map` is computed per element. Which you want changes the answer and the runtime.
verified: do { var n = 2 --- payload.x * n } with x=21 -> 42

units.title: Walk a tree of unknown depth
units.teaches: Writing a recursive function over nested data.
units.trap: The recursion has to test for the leaf case with `is Array` / `is Object` — there is no loop construct to fall back on.
verified: a recursive fun depth(v) compiles with NO return-type annotation and returns 3 for [[1,[2]]]
mutual recursion (two funs calling each other) also compiles with no return-type annotations

units.title: Touch every leaf, whatever the shape
units.teaches: `dw::util::Tree` — the module that does the generic walk for you.
units.trap: It is not in core; without the import the name simply does not resolve.
verified: import * from dw::util::Tree; mapLeafValues({a:{b:'x'},c:['y']}, (v,p) -> upper(v as String)) -> {a:{b:'X'},c:['Y']}

units.title: Enrich one list from another
units.teaches: `dw::core::Arrays` joins instead of a nested filter per row.
units.trap: `leftJoin` is not in core, and the inner join is called `join` — there is no `innerJoin`. The result is `{l: ..., r: ...}` pairs rather than merged objects, so merging them is part of the work.
verified: bare leftJoin -> CompilationException: Unable to resolve reference
dw_functions.json has join / leftJoin / outerJoin in module `arrays` — innerJoin does not exist
the signature declares the key lambdas return String, but Number keys match anyway at runtime — do NOT claim String is required

units.title: Field names that come from the data
units.teaches: Computed keys `(expr): value` and building an object from a list of pairs.
units.trap: A computed key needs the parentheses, and nothing stops two rows producing the same key — see duplicate-keys.
verified: computed keys via mapObject ((v,k,i) -> { (k): ... }) round-trip correctly

units.title: A SOAP body with namespaces
units.teaches: `ns` declarations and namespace-qualified selectors on input and output.
units.trap: A namespaced element does not match an unqualified selector, so the selector returns null and the mapping looks empty for no visible reason.

units.title: Totals that have to be exact
units.teaches: DataWeave numbers are arbitrary precision, not IEEE doubles.
units.trap: This one runs the other way: `0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3` is TRUE here, so habits carried from JavaScript or Java make people add rounding that is not needed — and that rounding is what introduces the error.

units.title: A summary report, two levels deep
units.teaches: Chaining groupBy → pluck → reduce into a report.
units.trap: After `groupBy` you are holding an object, so the next step has to be `pluck`/`mapObject`, not `map` — and `map` on an object does not fail loudly.

units.title: A fixed-width file from a mainframe
units.teaches: The flat-file reader and a schema with column widths.
units.trap: Padding is significant: the trim is yours to do, and a field read one column short is silently wrong rather than an error.

units.title: A CSV attachment inside a JSON envelope
units.teaches: `write` to embed one format inside another mid-transform.
units.trap: `write` gives you a String, so the result is an escaped blob — which is the point, and also why it looks broken the first time.
verified:
write([{price:3, sku:'F6', qty:4}], 'application/csv') -> "price,sku,qty
3,F6,4
" — column order follows the OBJECT's field order

units.title: Pass a rule in as an argument
units.teaches: Functions as values, partial application, `then` pipelines.
units.trap: Infix `then` rejects a named function as its callback — `10 then addN(5)` throws *Cannot coerce Function to String* — while the prefix form and an inline lambda both work.
verified: 10 then addN(5) -> UnsupportedTypeCoercionException: Cannot coerce Function to String

units.title: Declare the shape you expect
units.teaches: `type` declarations and checking a payload against one.
units.trap: `type` is a reserved word as a KEY, so a schema example that uses `type:` as a field name will not compile — quote it or rename it.
verified: { type: 'Odd' } -> CompilationException: The name `type` is a reserved word

units.title: Fail one record, not the batch
units.teaches: `dw::Runtime`'s `try` to contain a per-record failure.
units.trap: Without it, one bad coercion in one row aborts the entire transform.

units.title: Rename every key, everywhere, at any depth
units.teaches: A recursive transform over arbitrary JSON — snake_case to camelCase throughout.
units.trap: It has to handle objects, arrays, and scalars, and it must not rename the VALUES; most first attempts break on an array of scalars.

units.title: Nested orders out as flat CSV rows
units.teaches: One row per line item, with the parent's fields repeated.
units.trap: The row count comes from the children, so the parent fields have to be captured in scope before the inner map.

units.title: Rows into columns, columns unknown in advance
units.teaches: Building an object whose keys are discovered from the data.
units.trap: Rows missing a column must still emit it, or the CSV writer produces ragged lines from the first row's header.

units.title: Evaluate an expression tree
units.teaches: Recursion plus pattern matching: interpret `{op: '+', l: ..., r: ...}` down to a number.
units.trap: Mutual recursion and the leaf case; the type checker needs help once the function returns more than one type.

units.title: Validate a payload against a schema given as data
units.teaches: Walking two structures at once and collecting every error, not just the first.
units.trap: Accumulating errors across a recursive walk without a mutable variable is the whole problem.
